solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show anger, having damaged part of golf course

parts.note: something cut up has been slashed and damaged
the rough is the long grass bordering a golf fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer loses their temper after tearing up a patch of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become angry or aggressive, so it matches showing temper.

clue.text: Mafia boss entertains composer briefly for coffee

indicators.note: a host entertains a guest inside the home, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a capo is the head of a Mafia crime family

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Puccini is the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A gangster hosts an Italian composer over a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the composer's last letter, and 'entertains' splits the boss's title after its third letter to take him in.
explanation.definitionFit: This frothy espresso drink with steamed milk is a type of the beverage.

clue.text: Weight not to be lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word raises it so that it reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A heavy load that should not be raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is a unit of weight, equal to 2,240 pounds in Britain.

clue.text: Old astronomer finds temperature in arctic region? Gosh!

indicators.note: in places the temperature letter within the region's word

parts.note: the North Pole is the region at the top of the Arctic
my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: An astronomer measures the cold at the North Pole and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was the Alexandrian scholar of the second century whose earth-centred model of the heavens held for centuries.

clue.text: Fugitive no longer connected by marriage?

definitions.meaning: a fugitive is a lawless person on the run
a relative by marriage is an in-law, so one no longer related is whimsically 'out' instead of 'in'

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful one, marked by the question mark: flip the 'in' of in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit living beyond the reach of justice is on the run from the authorities.

clue.text: Rudely grab old film star

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so the letters of the word are knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone impolitely snatches at a veteran movie star.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Holding volunteer force, indeed wrongly arrested

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the shuffled letters surround the force's abbreviation
wrongly means incorrectly arranged, so the word's letters are reordered

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: The volunteer reserve is holding a suspect who was indeed wrongly arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' reorders the given word as DEINED, which 'Holding' wraps round the force. The Territorial Army was Britain's part-time army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect who is detained has been held in custody, which is what being arrested means.

clue.text: Fun for kids, dropping insect in river

indicators.note: in places the insect within the river's name

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
an ant is a small insect

explanation.surface: Children's fun is spoilt when an insect falls into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is the comic Christmas theatre entertainment traditionally aimed at children.

clue.text: Shortly go round important country

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to turn is to go round or rotate
a key point is an important one

explanation.surface: Reads as a terse instruction to tour an important nation soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is the nation spanning Anatolia and the far south-eastern corner of Europe.

clue.text: Poems about a sick palace

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the poems go round the other pieces

parts.note: verses are poems
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Verse written about an ailing royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the great French royal residence built by Louis XIV outside Paris.

clue.text: For audience, bring in big pot of tea

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners, so the word goes by how it sounds

parts.note: to earn is to bring in money

explanation.surface: A request to carry in a large teapot for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent EARN and URN sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea urn is a large metal vessel for serving hot water or brewed tea to a crowd.

clue.text: Author, strangely solvent one

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer who, oddly, has no debts.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of fiction books is one particular kind of author.

clue.text: European worried about work in America: it's complicated

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, work
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A European fretting over his US job finds it all very involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate, with many detailed parts, is complicated.

clue.text: Dropping some number, carries flocks of partridges

indicators.note: dropping means leaving out, so the number's letter is taken away

parts.note: conveys means carries
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Reads as birds being carried while some are dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number.
explanation.definitionFit: A covey is the collective noun for a small group of partridges or grouse.

clue.text: Managed university in America — it's another world!

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: Running a university in the US feels like being on a different planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus is the seventh planet from the sun, so it is a world other than ours.

clue.text: Curl right round fireplace

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes about the fireplace

parts.note: an ingle is an old word for a hearth or fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A curl of hair placed just to the right of the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral lock of hair.

clue.text: Notices a wide plank children play on

parts.note: sees means notices
W is the abbreviation for wide, an extra in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone spots a broad board at a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a balanced plank on which children ride up and down.

clue.text: Left engineer to relax in shade

indicators.note: letters that relax loosen their order and fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An engineer heads off to unwind in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to relax' rearranges L plus ENGINEER. 'Shade' looks like shelter from the sun, but it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green colour, named after the river.

clue.text: Chap installs lines for drain

indicators.note: installs means puts something in place inside, so the lines go within the chap

parts.note: a guy is a chap
L stands for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A workman lays pipes for a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a channel or gutter that carries water away, like a drain.

clue.text: Welshman finally paid fine

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, its last letter

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or fine, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A Welshman at last settled his fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written with the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David, used in crosswords for any Welshman.

clue.text: As afterthought, charity offers good book

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A charity tacks a postscript on to its offer of a fine book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good book' is lower case, but it points to the Good Book, the Bible, of which Psalms is one book.
explanation.definitionFit: The book of Psalms is one of the books of the Bible, the Good Book.

clue.text: Even raze to the ground

definitions.meaning: to raze a building is to flatten it completely

explanation.definitionFit: Flat ground is smooth and even, and knocking a building flat is to flatten it.

clue.text: Five of the Romans and one English compete

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Five Romans and one Englishman are in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to contend or strive against rivals.

clue.text: Sight-seer in court?

parts.note: a sightseer is a tourist, but read literally a 'seer' of a sight; one who saw an event and testifies in court

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'sightseer' into one who sees a sight, a person who saw a crime and gives evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who saw an incident with their own eyes and testifies to it in a trial is such a witness.
